clue.text: Parrot beginning to mimic a raven's cry

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the harsh call of a crow or raven

explanation.surface: A talking bird starts copying the call of a raven.
explanation.definitionFit: The macaw is a large, brightly coloured tropical American species of parrot.

clue.text: First to mention Egyptian god's greed

indicators.note: what comes first in a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: Ammon (Amun) was the chief god of ancient Thebes

explanation.surface: Someone is the first to point out that an Egyptian deity is grasping.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's on god belongs to the surface only; the wordplay just joins the letter to the god's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammon is the biblical personification of wealth, used for avarice and the worship of riches.

clue.text: Reportedly rough passage

indicators.note: what is reported is heard rather than read, so the word wanted only sounds like this one

explanation.surface: Word has it that a sea crossing was choppy.
explanation.definitionFit: A course is a route or way through, as a river's course is its passage.

clue.text: Dramatist, C. Marlowe, living rough close to playhouse

indicators.note: living rough means sleeping out in disorder, so the letters are tumbled into a new order
the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

explanation.surface: One Elizabethan playwright, Marlowe, is sleeping on the streets beside a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: Christopher Marlowe is a plausible dramatist for the definition, but his name is fodder; the answer is a Restoration playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: William Congreve wrote Restoration comedies such as The Way of the World, so he is a playwright.

clue.text: Sadly, sacked a dim clumsy servant

indicators.note: a sacked place has been ransacked and thrown into disorder
something clumsy is awkwardly put together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dull, ham-fisted domestic was regrettably dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' reads as a comment on the sacking but it is itself part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady's maid is a female domestic who attends personally to her mistress, a kind of servant.

clue.text: Listen and learn anew about Viking

indicators.note: doing something anew means doing it again differently, so these letters are made over
about means surrounding, so these letters wrap round another piece

explanation.surface: Pay attention and study the Norse raiders all over again.
explanation.definitionFit: To lend an ear is an idiom for paying attention to someone, that is, to hear them out.

clue.text: Doctor with a certain idle type

blocks.note: as in 'a certain person', one person

explanation.surface: A physician keeps company with a particular lazy individual.
explanation.definitionFit: A drone is a male bee that does no work, hence a figure for a loafer or parasite.

clue.text: Talking books meaning much

explanation.surface: Audiobooks that carry great significance.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking volumes is an idiom for conveying a great deal without saying it outright.

clue.text: Fabulous runner from area within US state capital

indicators.note: within places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: Atlanta is the capital of Georgia

explanation.surface: A superb athlete comes from somewhere in an American state capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' reads as praise, but it means 'of fable': the runner is a figure from Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend Atalanta was a swift huntress who raced her suitors and lost only to a trick with golden apples.

clue.text: Father on the way over in rowing boat, ridiculously inadequate

indicators.note: a thing going over is turned head to tail, so the word is read backwards
in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: a dory is a small flat-bottomed rowing boat
a sire is a father, especially of an animal

explanation.surface: A dad crossing the water in a small boat finds it laughably small.
explanation.definitionFit: A derisory sum is so small it invites derision, which is to say laughably insufficient.

clue.text: Foolishly tearful girl left at home

explanation.surface: A weepy young woman has been abandoned at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Maudlin means sentimentally self-pitying, given to tearful emotion, often from drink.

clue.text: Outdoor work drop of early rain ruined

indicators.note: a drop is a tiny amount, so just one letter, the first, is taken
something ruined is wrecked, its parts knocked out of order

blocks.note: op. is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: An outside event was spoiled by a spot of rain first thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop of early rain' reads as one weather phrase, but the drop is only the first letter of early; rain is fodder in full.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-air describes something held outside rather than under a roof, the same as outdoor.

clue.text: Stubborn old boy elected in republic

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a republic is a kind of state

explanation.surface: A pigheaded former pupil has won office in a republic.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstinate means refusing to change one's mind, a direct synonym of being pigheaded.

clue.text: Poet from Speke at service

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

blocks.note: letters running across the end of Speke, all of at and the start of service

explanation.surface: A poet comes from Speke, a Liverpool district, to attend church.
explanation.definitionFit: John Keats was an English Romantic poet, author of odes to a nightingale and autumn.

clue.text: One who usually makes a good impression?

definitions.text: One who usually makes a good impression?

blocks.clueFragment: One who usually makes a good impression?
blocks.note: surface reading: someone who tends to come across well to others
setter's reading: an impression is a mimicking act, and this performer does them well for a living

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that impression means an imitation of a celebrity, not a favourable effect on people.
explanation.definitionFit: An impersonator is an entertainer who mimics famous people, so the job is doing impressions.

clue.text: Sailor's pique about getting a gunpowder ingredient

blocks.note: an old salt is a seasoned sailor
a pet is a fit of sulking

explanation.surface: A seaman's sulk over something leads him to obtain explosive material.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre, potassium nitrate, is the oxidising component of black powder alongside charcoal and sulphur.

clue.text: Longs to nurse sick hero

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, as a baby is held in the arms

blocks.note: to ache for is to long for

explanation.surface: Someone yearns to look after an ailing champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles is the great Greek warrior of the Iliad, vulnerable only at his heel.

clue.text: Broadcast update about Italian's gift

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order
about means surrounding, so these letters go round another piece

blocks.note: It is short for Italian, as in gin and It (Italian vermouth)

explanation.surface: A news bulletin covers an Italian person's present.
explanation.definitionFit: An aptitude is a natural talent, which is what a gift for something means.

clue.text: Press delight in giving a hypocritical display of affection

blocks.note: a press is an old word for a cupboard, especially in Scotland and Ireland
to love something is to delight in it

explanation.surface: Journalists enjoy showing insincere fondness.
explanation.walkthrough: Press looks like the news media or a verb, but it is a dialect word for a cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupboard love is affection shown only to get something, as a pet fawns on whoever feeds it.

clue.text: Lizard again roaming around for all to see

indicators.note: roaming means wandering about, so the letters stray from their order
around means surrounding another piece

blocks.note: U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all audiences

explanation.surface: A reptile is out wandering once more in full view.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film classification for universal viewing.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguana is a large tropical American lizard with a spiny crest.

clue.text: Act as witness at critical trial

blocks.note: a test is a trial that decides something

explanation.surface: Someone gives evidence at a crucial court case.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness to something, declaring it true from one's own knowledge.

clue.text: It covers it, nice gateau, initially?

definitions.text: It covers it, nice gateau, initially?

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each preceding word

blocks.note: the first letters of the five words

explanation.surface: A question about what goes on top of a lovely cake.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of the answer: it is the sugar layer that covers a gateau.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing is the sweet coating spread over the top and sides of a cake.

clue.text: Of the highest quality, the stairs leading to the attic?

definitions.text: the stairs leading to the attic?

blocks.note: first meaning: first-rate, in the top rank

blocks.clueFragment: the stairs leading to the attic?
blocks.note: second meaning, read literally: the uppermost set of steps in a house

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful literal reading of the second half.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-flight means belonging to the best class, from the top division of a league; literally it is the highest staircase.

clue.text: Girl, useful person climbing

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing means reading from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: a valuable member of a team is an asset

explanation.surface: A young woman who is handy to have around is going up in the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Tessa is a girl's name, a short form of Theresa.

clue.text: Bay's fame

definitions.note: singular in the clue; the answer is the plural, bays

blocks.note: first meaning: the bay tree is the laurel
second meaning: honour won, from the laurel wreath of victory

explanation.walkthrough: Bay looks like a stretch of coast; it is the tree, whose leaves were woven into victors' wreaths.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurels are bay trees, and the plural also means renown, as in resting on one's laurels.

clue.text: Dish served up by one doctor in story

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A meal is brought out by a single physician in a narrative.
explanation.definitionFit: A timbale is a dish of minced meat or fish cooked in a drum-shaped mould or pastry case.

clue.text: Herts town boy, mature

explanation.surface: A grown-up lad from a Hertfordshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Herts is the abbreviation for Hertfordshire, a county just north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenage is a new town in Hertfordshire, built up after the Second World War.

clue.text: Astute, head of stock exchange

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: a mart is a market, a place of exchange

explanation.surface: The shrewd boss of the stock market.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart means clever and quick-witted, so shrewd in judgment like someone astute.
